evidence.excerpt:
We evaluate agent failures through a bifurcated methodology
that explicitly categorizes breakdowns into System-Level
errors and Task-Level errors. Because LLM agents op-
erate at the interface of programmatic tool execution and
probabilistic reasoning, this separation is essential to avoid
conflating deterministic infrastructure faults with semantic
cognitive limitations. Accordingly, our diagnostic pipeline
combines rule-based parsing to isolate System-Level errors
with a human-guided LLM-as-a-Judge framework to evalu-
ate Task-Level errors.

evidence.excerpt:
When infrastructure execution succeeds, agents may still
fail at the task level due to higher-order cognitive, strate-
gic, or synthesis limitations that emerge across extended
reasoning trajectories and large context windows. Because
these semantic breakdowns are difficult to capture through
rigid rule-based parsing alone, we adopt a human-guided
LLM-as-a-Judge pipeline to systematically interpret the ex-
ecution logs. To ensure our evaluation rubric is empirically
grounded rather than arbitrarily defined, we first conduct
a qualitative, human-in-the-loop analysis of sampled inter-
mediate traces to inductively construct a behavioral tax-
onomy. Building upon this foundation, we then employ
the LLM-as-a-Judge framework to automatically categorize
these process-level deviations at scale. Given the distinct
characteristics, we separately address the specific cognitive
bottlenecks

Although these benchmarks are traditionally employed for
end-to-end accuracy evaluation, our framework instead uses
them to generate complete execution traces. By leveraging
their curated task prompts, reference answers, and structural
requirements, we obtain standardized problem settings that
enable consistent, process-oriented error diagnosis across
diverse agent trajectories. We adopt GPT-5 as the LLM
judge for both system-level error and task-level error.

from both Deep Search and Deep Research settings under
the unified taxonomy introduced in Section 3. We first ana-
lyze System-Level errors to characterize interaction-side
reliability, and then analyze Task-Level errors to reveal
paradigm-specific cognitive bottlenecks in retrieval and syn-
thesis workflows. These results provide a fine-grained view

Task-Level Error. Task-level errors capture higher-order cog-
nitive and strategic failures that occur even when tool execu-
tion is syntactically valid. Unlike system-level breakdowns,
these errors are reflected in how agents explore, accumulate
evidence, and decide when to stop. In this section, we an-
alyze task-level error distributions across benchmarks and
models to identify paradigm-specific bottlenecks in Deep
Search and Deep Research workflows.
As detailed in Table 3, our task-level evaluation of Deep
Search agents reveals a strong positive correlation between
process-level reliability (No Error Rate) and final task accu-
racy (Acc). Models that successfully navigate intermediate
cognitive bottlenecks consistently achieve higher end-to-end
success, confirming the diagnostic validity of our taxonomy.

Broader Takeaway.Fine-grained evaluation serves as an
enabling infrastructure for reliable autonomous agents. By
transforming opaque failures into structured diagnostic sig-

tool ecosystems, and framework architecture. As agent au-

Our
work introduces a taxonomy aimed at more systematically
characterizing failure patterns in long-horizon, information-
dense autonomous research workflows.
B. Dataset
This appendix summarizes the dataset scale used in our
evaluation.
For Deep Search, we use four benchmarks: BrowseComp,
BrowseComp-zh, GAIA-val-text, and XBench-DS. Due to
evaluation cost constraints, BrowseComp and BrowseComp-
zh are evaluated using subsampled subsets.
For Deep Research, we use DeepResearch Bench as the
evaluation source for long-horizon synthesis tasks.
Success Criterion.For Deep Search, success is defined
by answer correctness against the ground truth. Given
model output ˆyand reference answer y∗, a run is con-
sidered successful when ˆymatches y∗ under benchmark
normalization rules (e.g., alias normalization and format-
ting tolerance). This criterion is relatively uniform across
Deep Search

For Deep Research, success criteria are benchmark-
dependent rather than uniform. In this work, we follow
the DeepResearch Bench (Du et al., 2025) setting and eval-
uate along two dimensions:
• RACE(Reference-based and Adaptive Criteria-driven
Evaluation)
– Comprehensiveness: coverage breadth and depth
of the research topic.
– Insight/Depth: quality of analysis and insight
generation.
– Instruction-Following: adherence to specific
task requirements.
– Readability: clarity, organization, and presenta-
tion quality.
• FACT(Factual Abundance and Citation Trustworthi-
ness)
– Citation Accuracy: percentage of correctly sup-
ported citations.
– Effective Citations: average number of verifiably
supported citations per task.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The reported correlation between process-level No Error Rate and external benchmark accuracy provides a measurement independent of the GPT-5 judge, and its direction supports the diagnostic validity claim.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Headline findings are error distributions and process-reliability statistics produced by rule-based parsing plus GPT-5 LLM-as-a-judge classification, with terminal accuracy from external benchmark ground truths.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: No agent or model is trained, tuned, selected, or otherwise adapted in this study; the work is a diagnostic benchmarking and error-analysis exercise over fixed agent frameworks and model backbones.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims regarding the prevalence and nature of intermediate execution errors are supported by quantitative step distributions, correlation with terminal accuracy, and qualitative case studies.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The framework is tested on multiple datasets (BrowseComp, BrowseComp-zh, GAIA, XBench-DS, and DeepResearch Bench) comparing different model architectures. The empirical analysis demonstrates clear differentiations in failure profiles across models and shows a strong correlation between process-level reliability and terminal accuracy.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: No optimization loop is performed; external benchmarks with ground-truth answers and standard evaluation criteria are used to measure final performance alongside error diagnosis.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Diagnostic classification of step traces using rule-based parsing and GPT-5 prompting alongside standard benchmark end-to-end task accuracy and report quality metrics.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: No models or agents were trained, tuned, or iteratively optimized against an internal metric in this benchmarking study.

primary.limitations: The work focuses on diagnostic categorization rather than online automated repair, evaluates a restricted toolset (search and fetch) in Deep Search, and relies partly on an LLM evaluator (GPT-5) for semantic task-level categorizations.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology combines rule-based structural parsing with human-guided LLM-as-a-judge prompting to classify step-by-step agent execution traces into granular categories (such as tool mismatch, premature stopping, and synthesis hallucination). Evaluated traces are collected under controlled agent setups across multiple standard benchmarks.
primary.quality_rationale: The study provides a clearly defined problem formulation, sound taxonomy, rigorous experimental trace diagnostics on established benchmarks, and actionable design insights for agent development, meeting the standards for scientific contribution.
primary.scoped_contribution: A diagnostic methodology and structured taxonomy categorizing intermediate execution errors of Deep Search and Deep Research LLM agents into system-level and task-level breakdowns across existing multi-step benchmarks.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The study provides a clearly defined problem formulation, sound taxonomy, rigorous experimental trace diagnostics on established benchmarks, and actionable design insights for agent development, meeting the standards for scientific contribution.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The work focuses on diagnostic categorization rather than online automated repair, evaluates a restricted toolset (search and fetch) in Deep Search, and relies partly on an LLM evaluator (GPT-5) for semantic task-level categorizations.

limitations_or_uncertainty.value: Structured research-card claims use title, abstract/summary, metadata, screening rules, and curation. A separate scholarly-quality assessment used bounded full-text excerpts, but unsupported claim, method, or evidence fields remain unextracted.
